summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain and increased lethargy. Workup revealed MRSA bacteremia and pneumonia, leading to a diagnosis of sepsis. She was started on IV vancomycin. A right lower leg fluid collection was evaluated with ultrasound and drained percutaneously; cultures were negative, consistent with a hematoma. Due to concern for her tunneled dialysis line as a source of infection, it was removed and replaced with a temporary line, followed by placement of a new tunneled line after clearance of bacteremia. Repeat blood cultures were negative, and she improved clinically. She was discharged home with plans for outpatient IV antibiotic completion and close follow-up.
problems: Sepsis due to Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus
